S1.label: Structured data reasoning
S1.notes: Agent misread or failed to correctly interpret reservation/order structured records — e.g., wrong flight prices, wrong item attributes, wrong passenger data in action arguments.

S2.label: Tool calling precision
S2.notes: Wrong tool arguments (wrong flight/item IDs, wrong payment methods, wrong counts/amounts) or calling the wrong tool entirely. The most pervasive failure mode across both domains.

S3.label: Multi-step completion
S3.notes: Agent failed to complete all required steps of a multi-part task — e.g., partial execution (cancelled only some reservations, modified only some orders), or missed a sequential action that depended on a prior one.

S4.label: Precondition verification
S4.notes: Agent violated or missed policy preconditions: cancelled flights that shouldn't be cancelled (no-refund cases), modified basic economy when forbidden, issued certificates for wrong reasons, or failed to refuse when policy blocked the action.

S5.label: Numerical reasoning
S5.notes: Wrong total amounts communicated or used in tool calls — incorrect refund calculations, incorrect payment splits, wrong certificate amounts (e.g., $300 vs $50, $150 vs correct amount), wrong price differences.

S6.label: Record discovery
S6.notes: Failed to locate the correct record (flight, order, user account, item variant) — called wrong order IDs, searched wrong product variant, failed to find user by name/zip, used wrong item IDs from product catalogue.

S7.label: Information communication
S7.notes: Failed to communicate specific required facts: wrong refund amount stated, tracking number not given, item material/specs not reported, certificate amount wrong in verbal response.

S8.label: Conditional/state reasoning
S8.notes: Agent failed to reason about conditional branching tasks or current order/reservation state — e.g., 'if X is not possible do Y', failed to recognize basic economy restrictions apply to modification, failed to determine correct cancellation based on current status.

S9.label: Language fluency
S9.notes: No clear evidence of fluency failures in failed tasks.

S11.label: Tone/empathy
S11.notes: Agent was manipulated by emotional framing — changed a basic economy flight for a grieving user (T36) or stayed in jailbreak loop without redirecting (T9). In retail, sycophantic drift around emotional/angry users delayed or altered correct actions.

S12.label: Hallucination of tools
S12.notes: No clear evidence of hallucinated tool calls in failed tasks.

S13.label: Format compliance
S13.notes: R76: 'The number of items to be exchanged should match' error — agent passed mismatched item arrays to exchange tool, indicating incorrect formatting of the tool call payload.

S14.label: Context window mgmt
S14.notes: Tasks that terminated due to max_steps — agent looped on errors (payment calculation loop in A42, jailbreak loop in A9, complex multi-order search in R104), failing to resolve within the turn budget.

S15.label: Multilingual handling
S15.notes: A39 had a French-speaking user but the failure was due to wrong cancellation logic (S4/S3), not language comprehension. No pure language failures observed.

S16.label: Proactive upselling
S16.notes: No upselling failures observed; upselling is not required in these tasks.
